title: Fakipedia: Building and exploiting an AI model for detecting online fake news in Burkina Faso
abstract: Misinformation poses a significant challenge, especially in developing countries with low literacy rates. The rapid spread on social media, coupled with their lack of robust verification mechanisms, makes distinguishing between credible and false information increasingly difficult. This document outlines our efforts to address this challenge in Burkina Faso using the pre-trained linguistic model CAMEMBERT. Our preliminary results show high performance (up to a 99.34% F1 score) on Fakipedia.

title: Evaluating Acoustic Parameters for DeepFake Detection in Audio Signals
abstract: This study evaluates acoustic parameters for detecting deepfake audio signals, analyzing spectral and temporal features to distinguish authentic from synthetic speech. Results show high accuracy using MFCC and pitch variation metrics.

title: Text-to-OWL: Automated Ontology Construction from Natural Language Text
abstract: Presents an automated pipeline converting unstructured text into OWL ontologies using NLP and transformer-based models. Evaluated on domain-specific corpora with promising precision and recall scores.

title: Voice Interaction in Moore Language: A Speech Recognition Approach
abstract: Proposes a speech recognition system adapted to the Moore language, addressing data scarcity with transfer learning and data augmentation techniques. Achieves competitive word error rates.

title: Detecting Illicit Data Leaks on Android Applications
abstract: Introduces a static and dynamic analysis framework for detecting unauthorized data exfiltration in Android apps, identifying sensitive API misuse and network leaks across a large app corpus.

title: AI-Based Approach for Early Diagnosis of Hemorrhagic Stroke
abstract: A hemorrhagic stroke is a life-threatening medical condition that happens when a blood vessel in your brain ruptures and bleeds. The current definitive diagnosis is based on brain scanning and AI-assisted methods are explored to accelerate detection.
